purpose: Preregistered synthetic diagnostic and artifact review cases, not model results. All criteria require semantic review.

criteria: Withdraw the unsupported absence-to-route conclusion while preserving its record and identifying affected decisions.
Recognize the narrow diagnostic misses known positives and the wide diagnostic has false positives; neither justifies the claimed absence or physical coverage.
Separate reproduction of cleanup decisions from independently known ray geometry; removed and retained labels are not automatically physical ground truth.
Propose representative positive and negative controls with geometry- and uncertainty-based settings, bounded sensitivity checks and independent confirmation; do not widen until everything passes.
Keep the physical cause unresolved and report diagnostic scope instead of claiming the opposite conclusion is proven.
Distinguish helper execution from caller selection and saved-output adoption; retain the acceptance failure and check the saved artifact read-only.
Identify equal counts with unequal removed-ID sets; compare both differences on the same input universe.
Treat resampled radius matches as approximate and account for duplicate multiplicity and identity loss.
Do not infer historical ancestry from coordinate equality without processing records; state the missing lineage evidence.
Distinguish different binary bytes from tested behavioral equivalence on one corpus, without a universal equivalence or hardware-readiness claim.
Explain why fixed contributions, a fixed universe and a monotone final union make A subset-dominant, duplicate-idempotent and order-independent.
Compute B outputs as {0}, {4,5}, and {4,5}; reject a general subset-dominance or order-independence claim based only on a set-only flag.
Check whole-pipeline preprocessing, poses, grid, adaptive choices, resets and final query before transferring the proof to another implementation.
Keep bounded prefix tests for marginal contribution, cost or sufficiency even when a subset cannot beat A on final removal count.
Reopen B because the doorway rejection did not measure the requirement; preserve and correct the earlier record rather than treating it as settled.
Report target and preservation metrics with denominators: A=20% and 0.1%, B=30% and 0.15%, C=95% and 30%.
Reject C under the stated 1% static-deletion constraint rather than optimizing only person removal.
Treat B as supported on the exploratory recording, not confirmed for all maps; freeze criteria and require independent confirmation.
Do not deploy a map or claim physical safety from offline results; distinguish retracted decisions from remaining uncertainty.
